title: Built in 1553 CE
description: Bahadur Singh commissioned the surviving shrine in 1553. The sanctuary encloses a natural rock associated with local worship; epic traditions are not treated as construction dates.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Approximately 8th century CE
description: The monolithic complex belongs to the early medieval period. Earthquake damage and unfinished portions remain part of its architectural history; a securely identified royal commissioner is not recorded here.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Founded in 996 CE; later additions
description: The monastery was founded in 996 under western Tibetan royal patronage. Its painted interiors and later buildings represent several phases, rather than one unchanged tenth-century structure.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Approximately 11th–13th-century temple phases
description: The Alchi religious complex preserves early western Himalayan Buddhist art. The dates refer to its historic temple phases; attribution to a single founder or dynasty remains qualified.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Founded in the 15th century; later growth
description: The Gelug monastery developed on a hill near Leh. Its foundation and the many later structures should be read as different phases; the record does not assign the whole complex to one royal patron.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Surviving stone phase, approximately 12th–13th centuries
description: ASI distinguishes evidence of earlier brick and wooden members from the surviving stone temple, which it places in the twelfth–thirteenth centuries. Popular early foundation dates are not applied to every surviving component.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Approximately 17th century CE
description: The funerary ensemble includes two tombs, a madrasa and gardens. Its seventeenth-century Mughal context is recorded separately from uncertain biographical identifications of the saint.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Principal civic buildings, 1950s–1960s
description: Le Corbusier and collaborators designed the civic ensemble after Indian independence. It is included as a documented modern heritage exception, not as architecture of an ancient empire.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: 18th-century fort; Sikh-period expansion
description: The fort passed from the Bhangi Misl to Maharaja Ranjit Singh and later British control. Sikh-period strengthening is recorded as an addition, not as the first construction of every wall.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Approximately 1650 CE
description: Prince Dara Shukoh developed the terraced garden around 1650 during Shah Jahan's reign. Its documented Mughal patronage does not establish the date of every surviving repair.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Reign of Avantivarman, 855–883 CE
description: Avantivarman of the Utpala dynasty commissioned the ninth-century shrine. The record concentrates on the Avantiswami precinct rather than treating nearby temples as one building.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Major Koch rebuilding, 1565 CE; older origins
description: The shrine has earlier origins and repeated rebuilding. Koch ruler Naranarayan is associated with the major sixteenth-century reconstruction; later additions form part of its layered history.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Reign of Pramatta Singha, 1744–1751 CE
description: The Ahom royal pavilion served as a viewing place for games and gatherings near the former Rangpur capital. Its masonry phase belongs to the eighteenth century.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Royal burial landscape, 13th–19th centuries
description: The Ahom royal necropolis developed over centuries. UNESCO inscribed the property in 2024; that recognition date is separate from the construction and use of the burial mounds.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: World Heritage inscription
description: UNESCO inscribed the Moidams in 2024. Recognition is separate from the centuries of burial construction and use.
locator: Date of inscription

title: Royal seat until 1891
description: The official district history identifies Kangla as the seat of Manipur rulers until 1891. This is a change in royal use, not a construction date.
locator: Historical use of Kangla

title: Built 1899–1901 CE
description: Maharaja Radha Kishore Manikya commissioned the palace in 1899–1901. It later accommodated the state legislature and now serves as a museum.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Built 1930–1938 CE
description: Bir Bikram Kishore Manikya built the lake palace as a summer residence during 1930–1938. Its princely patronage is distinct from an attribution to Mughal imperial rule.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Early foundation; expansion in 1705–1710 CE
description: Founded as an early religious establishment, the monastery was enlarged under Sikkim's Chogyal rulers. Sources distinguish its seventeenth-century beginnings from eighteenth-century expansion.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Capital in use, 1670–1814 CE
description: Rabdentse served as a capital of the Namgyal kingdom of Sikkim. The date range describes the capital's period of use, not a continuous construction campaign.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Approximately 13th–14th-century temple phase
description: The archaeological site preserves a medieval temple and sculptural remains. Arunachal Tourism associates the phase with Chutiya rulers; this is a qualified historical attribution.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Approximately 11th century CE
description: The main stone Shiva shrine forms part of a group that also includes earlier and later monuments. Its medieval architecture is associated with the region's Nagavanshi rulers.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Approximately 7th century CE
description: Queen Vasata commissioned the Vishnu shrine in memory of Harshagupta in the Panduvamshi period. It belongs to Sirpur's wider, multi-religious archaeological landscape.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Temple-building phases, 17th–19th centuries
description: The village's patron families sponsored successive temples rather than one unified royal palace. Sources associate the temple-building tradition with the Baj Basanta family.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Founded in 1691 CE; later reconstruction
description: The original hilltop shrine was founded in the seventeenth century under local Nagvanshi patronage. Parts of the present building reflect reconstruction after a twentieth-century collapse.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Built 1540–1545 CE
description: Sher Shah Suri's mausoleum was completed in 1545 during the Sur dynasty. Its commemorative function and completion are distinguished from the emperor's earlier political career.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Built 1829–1837 CE
description: Nawab Humayun Jah commissioned the palace, designed by Duncan MacLeod. Its European architectural vocabulary does not erase the agency of its Nawabi patron.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Reliefs stylistically dated to 8th–9th centuries
description: The reliefs predate Manikya rule. UNESCO's tentative-list account dates them stylistically to the eighth–ninth centuries; a specific royal patron is not established.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Approximately 950–975 CE
description: The tenth-century Shiva shrine occupies an important place in the development of Odisha temple architecture. A dynastic-period association is not treated as proof of a named commissioner.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Unfinished 11th-century temple
description: The unfinished Shiva temple is associated with Paramara ruler Bhoja. Nearby quarry marks and architectural drawings are important evidence of its construction process.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Early 17th century; sources cite 1614 and 1620
description: Bir Singh Deo commissioned the palace. Official accounts give differing early-seventeenth-century dates, retained here as an uncertainty range rather than one exact construction year.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Approximately 6th century CE
description: The Vishnu shrine belongs to the Gupta-period architectural tradition. Its surviving reliefs and platform are early evidence of a developed structural temple plan.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Late 15th–early 16th-century work
description: Queen Rudabai's patronage is associated with the late-fifteenth-century stepwell. The monument belongs to a regional setting shaped by both local rulers and the Gujarat Sultanate.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Harappan settlement phases, approximately 2400–1600 BCE
description: Lothal formed part of the Indus civilisation's settlement and trade network. The function of the large basin is discussed in archaeological interpretation; it is not presented here as an undisputed dock.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Major Maratha capital phase, 1656–1680 CE
description: Shivaji adapted the earlier hill fort as a Maratha capital and held his coronation there in 1674. Its history includes earlier occupation and later military events.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: 12th-century origins; later sultanate phases
description: The Yadava stronghold became the Delhi Sultanate's capital during Muhammad bin Tughluq's fourteenth-century transfer. Later Deccan rulers adapted the extensive defences.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Built 1664–1667 CE
description: Shivaji commissioned the island fort in the seventeenth century as part of Maratha coastal defence. The fort forms part of the Maratha Military Landscapes property inscribed in 2025.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Major surviving military phases, 16th–18th centuries
description: Gingee passed through Nayaka, Maratha, Mughal and other phases. It is not attributed wholesale to one emperor; Maratha adaptation is one documented layer.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Approximately mid-17th-century fort phase
description: Kerala Tourism associates the fort's principal construction with Shivappa Nayaka of Ikkeri. Later control by Mysore belongs to a separate historical phase.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Early medieval phases; sources differ between 5th and 7th centuries
description: The caves preserve early medieval religious and architectural phases. Accounts differ on chronology and patronage, so the range remains broad and dynastic connections qualified.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Conventionally dated to 1163 CE
description: Rudra Deva commissioned the twelfth-century Kakatiya shrine. Its familiar name is not used as an independently verified count of every surviving pillar.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Principal construction, 1562–1619 CE
description: The cathedral developed under Portuguese rule in Goa. Construction, consecration and later alterations are separate stages rather than a single date.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Fort construction, approximately 1588–1594 CE
description: Raja Rai Singh's fort became the core of a palace ensemble enlarged by later Bikaner rulers. The dates describe the initial fort phase, not every decorated room.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Medieval fort with successive later phases
description: The fort changed hands among regional Rajput rulers and later powers. Its inclusion in the Hill Forts of Rajasthan property recognizes the landscape-based defensive ensemble.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Portuguese construction and strengthening, 1535–1546 CE
description: The Portuguese developed the fort following an agreement with Gujarat's Sultan Bahadur Shah. Subsequent strengthening belongs to the wider sixteenth-century military history of Diu.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase

title: Early 20th-century construction phase
description: The Catholic church developed in the early twentieth century in French-administered Pondicherry. Its religious patronage is distinguished from a claim that the French state commissioned the building.
locator: Historical chronology; date applies only to the described phase
